title: Shackleton and the Endurance — 28 men, two years in the ice, nobody died
sources: Wikipedia: Imperial Trans-Antarctic Expedition — Endurance left South Georgia on 5 December 1914 to cross Antarctica; by January 1915 she was beset in the pack ice of the Weddell Sea and drifted north through the Antarctic winter; on 27 October 1915, at −22 to −27 °C, Shackleton ordered 'abandon ship'; the ice crushed her and on 21 November 1915 she sank; the 28 men camped on drifting ice floes for months; on 9 April 1916 the floe split and they took to three lifeboats, reaching Elephant Island on 15 April — the first landing ever made there; on 24 April Shackleton and five men sailed the 22.5-foot James Caird about 800 miles (1,300 km) across the Southern Ocean to South Georgia; Shackleton, Worsley and Crean then crossed the unmapped mountains of South Georgia in 36 hours and reached the Stromness whaling station on 20 May 1916; it took four attempts to return for the men on Elephant Island; on 30 August 1916 the Chilean tug Yelcho rescued all of them. The famous 'men wanted' advertisement is generally regarded as apocryphal. Wikipedia: Endurance (1912 ship) — the wreck was found on 5 March 2022 at 3,008 m, in 'a brilliant state of preservation'.

Photos (public domain, Wikimedia Commons / State Library of New South Wales / Royal Geographical Society): photographs by Frank Hurley, 1914–1916 — Endurance under sail and trapped in the ice, the final sinking, Shackleton and Wild, the boats on Elephant Island, launching the James Caird, the rescue by the Yelcho; Shackleton portrait by Hurley, 1916
Archive film (public domain): 'The Great White Silence' (Herbert Ponting, 1924) — Antarctic expedition footage of the same era, illustrative, not the Endurance
Music: Grieg, Piano Concerto — Adagio, public domain

post.facebook:
28 men were trapped in the Antarctic ice for almost two years. Not one of them died.

In December 1914, Ernest Shackleton sailed for Antarctica on Endurance, planning to be the first to cross it on foot. They never even landed: the sea froze around the ship and held her like a fist. For ten months they drifted with the ice through the polar winter. Then the ice began to crush her — "abandon ship" — and a month later they watched Endurance sink.

They camped on floating ice for five months, eating seals and penguins. When the ice split under them, they rowed three lifeboats to a frozen rock called Elephant Island. No one would ever look for them there, so Shackleton took five men in a seven-metre lifeboat and sailed 1,300 km across the worst ocean on Earth to South Georgia — landing on the wrong side. Three of them then crossed unmapped mountains for 36 hours to reach a whaling station.

It took Shackleton four attempts to get back through the ice. On 30 August 1916, a Chilean tug reached Elephant Island: every single man was alive. And in 2022, Endurance was found 3 km down, almost perfectly preserved.

Greatest leader in history? 🧊

youtube.description:
28 men were trapped in the Antarctic ice for almost two years. Not one of them died.

Ernest Shackleton's ship Endurance was trapped and crushed by the Weddell Sea ice in 1915. The crew camped on drifting floes, reached Elephant Island in three lifeboats, and Shackleton sailed 1,300 km in the 7-metre James Caird to South Georgia, crossed its mountains on foot, and after four attempts rescued every man on 30 August 1916. The wreck was found in 2022, 3 km down.
